subject: Architecture recap + embedder pipeline guardrails & next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jackson <sam.jackson@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Architecture recap + embedder pipeline guardrails & next steps

Hi Sam / Aisha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so your engineering team has a single reference. I’ve attached: redwood_sow_v1.pdf (high-level SOW) and schema-proposal.yaml (initial structured-output definitions).

Recap (high level)
- Goal: Integrate Redwood inference for two features — (1) semantic search embeddings + reranker, (2) structured tool-calling responses for domain object extraction.
- Scope for PoC: SDK bootstrap (node/python), auth (short-lived API keys via your KMS OR OAuth client), routing to regional endpoints, and structured-output enforcement with retry/fallback behavior.

Technical priorities & constraints we captured
- Latency target: 150ms p50 on text gen + reranker end-to-end for 90th percentile of queries.
- Data residency: US-only; we’ll use us-west and fall back to us-east if capacity constraints occur.
- Safety: Schema validation must be enforced before ingestion into your downstream systems.

Proposed integration guardrails (short list)
1) SDK setup & auth
   - Use the Redwood SDK (node/python) bundled with a validation hook. We recommend short-lived API keys minted via your KMS, rotated daily. OAuth is available if you want user-bound tokens.
2) Routing & fallbacks
   - Primary: us-west inference pool; fallback policy: us-east compatible model variant. Canary 10% traffic before full cutover.
3) Structured output & tool-calling
   - Enforce a JSON schema at the SDK boundary (schema-proposal.yaml). If the model output fails validation:
       a) Attempt constrained-decoding pass (prompted re-run with higher decoding constraints).
       b) If still invalid after 2 attempts, emit a deterministic error payload + raw text in a quarantine queue for manual review.
4) Embeddings + reranker pipeline
   - Batch embedder calls, persist vectors in your vector DB (we recommend ~512 dims quantized). Reranker runs a lightweight re-score using model logits; Redwood provides a reranker endpoint prototype.
5) Observability
   - Token-level cost, schema-rejection rate, constrained-decode attempts, and p50/p95 latency per model variant.

Next steps (action items)
- Your side: confirm KMS choice and whether you prefer API keys or OAuth by Fri 8/13.
- Redwood: technical SOW update (attached) and a scoped PoC timeline (we can spin up a dedicated sandbox).

Can we lock a 45-minute follow-up next week to align on the PoC milestones and the sandbox credentials? I’m available Tue/Thu mornings PT.

Thanks,

Thanks, Olga — great summary. A few clarifying questions before we circle on the PoC timeline: 

1) Embedding latency: our vector store is latency-sensitive. When you say "batch embedder calls," what batching window do you recommend and how does that affect p50?
2) Constrained decoding: does Redwood provide a built-in constrained-decoding mode that guarantees schema conformance, or is the validation + re-run loop something we implement at the SDK layer?
3) Failover behavior: if we hit model capacity in us-west and failover to us-east variant, is there any semantic drift risk (different tokenizer/quantization) you’ve observed?

If you can call out answers to those items, we can confirm internal stakeholders and pick Tues (8/17) 10am PT for the follow-up. Also — please send a slightly edited SOW with a clear PoC success criteria section.

Subject: Re: Architecture recap + embedder pipeline guardrails & next steps

Hi Sam / Aisha — quick technical answers and a small implementation sketch to unblock your eng review.

1) Embedding batching and latency-recommendation
- For online low-latency lookup: aim for per-request embedding (no batching) or micro-batches of 16 requests if you can accept ~20ms extra p50.
- For indexing or backfill: max batch sizes 256–1024 with async workers. Redwood’s embedder supports dynamic batching; you configure max_batch_size and max_wait_ms.

2) Constrained decoding & schema enforcement
- Redwood provides two orthogonal controls: (A) decode-time constraints (beam/nucleus+token-blocking templates + tool-calling tokens suppressed) and (B) SDK-level schema validation hooks.
- We do not guarantee 100% conformance from a single decode pass in all cases (edge cases exist), so we recommend the two-stage approach: run a constrained decode pass, validate against schema-proposal.yaml, and if it fails, re-run with stronger constraints and a fixed seed. After N attempts (we default to 2), the SDK emits a structured error with raw model output persisted to quarantine.

Sample SDK flow (pseudo)
1) call = client.generate(prompt, schema_hint=schema-proposal.yaml, decode_profile="constrained")
2) if validate(call.output, schema): return call.output
3) else: call2 = client.generate(prompt, decode_profile="constrained+strict", seed=42)
4) if validate(call2.output, schema): return call2.output
5) else: write_quarantine({request, call.output, call2.output, validation_errors}) and return {error_code: "SCHEMA_FAIL", raw: call2.output}

3) Failover semantic drift
- Risk: model variant differences (quantization & tokenizer) can change whitespace/float formatting for numeric fields and subtle string tokenization. Mitigations we recommend:
  - Use the same model family across regions when possible (e.g., rw-llama-2-13b in us-west and the mirrored 13b in us-east).
  - Normalization step in the SDK for numeric/date formats before validation.
  - Add a small tolerance for floating fields in the schema (e.g., numeric with epsilon).

Operational notes
- Observability: instrument the SDK to emit metric tags: schema_validation.{pass,fail}, constrained_decode.attempts, fallback.region.
- Performance: quantized embedder reduces memory and latency but may hurt similarity slightly; we can trial 8-bit quantization in the sandbox.

I’ll prepare a short PoC runbook and drop it in the Drive folder referenced in Olga's email. Proposed PoC milestones:
- Day 0–3: SDK bootstrapping & auth (sandbox creds)
- Day 4–8: Basic pipeline (embed -> store, generate -> validate)
- Day 9–12: Reranker integration + SLAs/observability
- Day 13–15: Acceptance & success criteria verification

Attached: small sample schema + quickstart snippets in the Drive link.
